newsitem.title: HUNGARY: EGIS OPENS STEADY AFTER NEWS OF POLISH DEAL.
newsitem.headline: EGIS OPENS STEADY AFTER NEWS OF POLISH DEAL.

text.p: Shares in Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Egis Gyogyszergyar Rt opened steady on Thursday, after a newspaper report that Egis and its French owner bought a Polish pharmaceuticals company.
Egis shares opened at 14,300 forints, unchanged from Wednesday's close. At 0955 GMT it traded at 14,255 forints.
Egis's Vice President for Finance, Laszlo Marosffy told Reuters the information in the economic daily Napi Gazdasag this morning was correct.
The newspaper said Egis, together with its majority owner, France's Servier S.A., bought a Polish drugs company, the name of which was not revealed.
However, the newspaper said the company had sales last year amounting to around $5 million and had a strong market position in generic products.
The newspaper added that Servier has an over 50 percent stake in the Polish firm, and therefore the Polish company would therefore not be fully consolidated into Egis's earnings.
Marosffy declined to give more details but reiterated that once legal proceedings of the deal are closed, Egis will provide more information.
Napi Gazdasag said the proceedings are expected to be finished in August.
